pages.description: Interactive English practice for Grades 6 to 11, with three activities for each grade built from the competency levels of the school syllabus for that grade.
pages.keywords: grade 6 english, grade 7 english, grade 8 english, grade 9 english, grade 10 english, grade 11 english, competency levels, syllabus practice, Sri Lanka

hero.text: Interactive English practice for Grades 6 to 11. Each grade provides three interactive language activities and five complete listening tests, every one of them aligned with a numbered competency level from the syllabus that grade actually follows. Everything marks itself and explains the answer.

blocks.title: Where these activities come from
text: Every activity on these pages is built from **the competency levels of the school syllabus**, not from examination papers. Each one names the competency level it practises, so you can check it against your own term notes.

Note that Grades 6 and 7 are not following the same syllabus. **Grade 6 has moved to the new 2026 syllabus**, which is organised by skill — listening, speaking, reading, writing and literary appreciation — and is grouped around text types rather than grammar topics. **Grades 7 to 11 remain on the earlier syllabus**, built around eight competencies covering sounds, mechanics of writing, listening, vocabulary, reading, grammar, written communication and speaking.
This matters when comparing grades: the same number means different things on either side of that line. Competency level 5.4 in Grade 8 is not competency level 5.4 in Grade 6.

The listening tests are read aloud using the English voice your own device provides, so the voices may sound different on a computer and on a phone. The words and the questions are the same everywhere.

items.title: Grade 6
items.text: Reading a timetable, filling in a form, and a simple poem. Listening: conversations, an announcement and a story. New 2026 syllabus.

items.title: Grade 7
items.text: Past and future continuous, modals, and joining words. Listening: directions, announcements and spoken instructions.

items.title: Grade 8
items.text: The past perfect, the passive voice, and reflexive pronouns. Listening: a weather forecast, a process and a spoken report.

items.title: Grade 9
items.text: Passive past and future, reported statements, and reading between the lines. Listening: interviews, and inferring what is implied.

items.title: Grade 10

items.title: Grade 11
items.text: All three conditionals, reported questions and commands, and word class. Listening: a debate, a committee meeting and an interview.

pages.keywords: grade 6 english, new 2026 syllabus, functional text, form filling, simple poem, competency levels

hero.text: Grade 6 follows the new 2026 syllabus, which is organised by skill rather than by grammar topic. These activities cover listening, reading a functional text, writing in an official context, and reading a literary text. Each one names the competency level it practises.

blocks.title: Grade 6 is on the new syllabus
text: From 2026, Grade 6 works to a syllabus organised around five competencies — listening, speaking, reading, writing and literary appreciation — with texts grouped as functional, informational or literary. The competency numbers here do not match those used in Grades 7 to 11.

blocks.heading: Grade 6 English practice
intro: Reading a timetable, filling in a form, and reading a simple poem. These follow competency levels 3.1, 3.2, 3.5, 3.6 and 4.1 of the 2026 syllabus.

blocks.heading: Grade 6 listening practice
intro: Five complete listening tests: short conversations, an announcement, a description and a story. The passage is read aloud by your own browser, so there is nothing to download.

Choose **Practice** to replay as often as you like, or **Formal test** for examination conditions, where the recording plays twice only. You can change the reading speed, and the transcript appears only after you submit. These follow competency levels 1.1 to 1.6 of the 2026 syllabus.

hero.text: Grade 8 is where the passive voice is introduced. The syllabus sets it in the simple present, simple past and simple future across Terms 2 and 3, alongside the past perfect. Get these right here and Grades 9 and 10 become much easier.

blocks.heading: Grade 8 grammar practice
intro: The past perfect tense, the passive voice in the simple tenses, and reflexive pronouns. These follow competency levels 6.1 and 6.2.

blocks.heading: Grade 8 listening practice
intro: Five complete listening tests: a weather forecast, advice at a dental clinic, an explanation of how paper is made, a project report and a booking made by telephone.

Choose **Practice** to replay freely, or **Formal test** for examination conditions. The transcript appears only after you submit. These follow competency levels 3.2 to 3.4, and the paper-making test also practises the passive voice from competency level 6.1.

hero.text: Grade 9 extends the passive voice and introduces reported speech. It also asks something new of readers: working out what a text implies but never actually says. That last skill carries marks right through to O/L.

blocks.heading: Grade 9 English practice
intro: The passive voice in past and future, reported statements, and reading between the lines. These follow competency levels 6.1, 6.11, 5.7 and 5.8.

blocks.heading: Grade 9 listening practice
intro: Five complete listening tests: two interviews, a talk, and two conversations in which the speakers' feelings are suggested rather than stated.

Choose **Practice** to replay freely, or **Formal test** for examination conditions. The transcript appears only after you submit. These follow competency levels 3.3, 3.4 and 3.6, and the two conversations practise inference at competency levels 5.7 and 5.8.

hero.text: Grade 10 completes the passive voice. Having met it in the simple tenses at Grade 8 and the past and future at Grade 9, the syllabus now works through every perfect and continuous form. O/L preparation begins here in earnest.

blocks.heading: Grade 10 grammar practice

blocks.heading: Grade 10 listening practice

Choose **Practice** to replay freely, or **Formal test** for examination conditions. The transcript appears only after you submit. These follow competency levels 3.4, 3.6, 3.7 and 3.8.

hero.text: The O/L year. Grade 11 consolidates rather than introduces: the conditionals are brought together, reported speech is extended to questions and commands, and word building is revisited. All three are areas where marks are thrown away by habit rather than by difficulty.

blocks.heading: Grade 11 grammar practice
intro: Conditional clauses of all types, reported questions and commands, and changing the class of a word. These follow competency levels 6.10, 6.11, 4.4 and 4.7.

blocks.heading: Grade 11 listening practice
intro: Five complete listening tests at the hardest level on the site: a formal debate, a careers talk, an interview in which much is implied, a committee meeting, and examination advice.

Choose **Practice** to replay freely, or **Formal test** for examination conditions. The transcript appears only after you submit. These follow competency levels 3.6, 3.7 and 3.8, with inference at 5.7 and 5.8.
